name: Chablis

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Chardonnay sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.

keyfacts: Chablis has four levels: Petit Chablis, Chablis, Premier Cru and Grand Cru, with Chablis AOC designated in 1938 and Petit Chablis in 1944.
Chablis must be made from Chardonnay alone, and typically shows much less oak influence than the white wines of the rest of Burgundy.
All Grand Cru and Premier Cru vineyards are on Kimmeridgean soil, which gives a mineral, flinty note, while most Petit Chablis is on younger Portlandian soil.
The seven Grand Cru vineyards lie on one southwest-facing hill above the town: Bougros, Les Preuses, Vaudésir, Grenouilles, Valmur, Les Clos and Blanchot.
Spring frost from March to early May is a major risk, and protection includes smudge pots and sprinklers that coat the vines in ice.

blurb.text: A Burgundy appellation in the far north of the region, making dry white wine from Chardonnay alone. The cool climate gives high acidity and less fruitiness, often with a flinty or steely note, and oak influence is usually much lighter than elsewhere in Burgundy.
